minutes.headline: Parks Commission agreed to require a performance-type bond from the skate park group and approved signing the Marshall Park septic permit filing.
minutes.summary: The commission heard resident comment on beach operations, voted to let the chair sign the conservation filing for the Marshall Park septic repair, and discussed the skate park project at length, reaching consensus that some form of bond will be required. It also discussed beach season preparation, hiring and lifeguard pay, portable toilets (no action taken), and a possible dog run. January minutes were held over.

budget_items.what_was_said: Funding for replacing the leaking front wall is undetermined; it could come from the DPW facilities line or the parks revolving fund.
The chair asked the recreation director to verify lifeguard pay is at or above minimum wage; a range was mentioned from memory.
Members said the beach lifeguard line runs in the red and asked the town to explain how the revolving account can cover salaries; they favored holding fees at the status quo.
Members noted cash must be accepted by law and asked for a point-of-sale system with cash procedures so staff do not fund a petty cash drawer.

Three quotes were obtained for units at several parks, expected to be paid from the revolving account; trash container add-on also quoted. Other members doubted usage and cost recovery from little league.

budget_items.topic: Skate park performance and payment bonds
budget_items.what_was_said: A bond would cost the skate park group extra; members favored a bond covering completion or restoration of the site to avoid prevailing-wage costs to the town.
Greg offered to get ballpark numbers for sewer hookup and noted ledge adds cost; the board of health has money for the septic repair.
The town manager sent a list of tax lien properties; members noted taking them would lose tax revenue and did not pursue them.

decisions.decision: The chair confirmed the beach will accept cash this year.

Consensus of the four commissioners that the skate park group will be required to provide a bond (completion or site restoration); the chair will ask the town manager what the restoration bond would be called and report back.
January 4th/6th and January 20th draft minutes held until members have reviewed them, aiming for the March meeting.
Recreation director asked to verify lifeguard pay versus minimum wage so the personnel committee can be approached if needed.
No action on portable toilets at all parks; commission preferred to wait for summer programming plans.
Marshall Park survey held until funding source is voted; chair to circulate it around late February break.
Next commission meeting set for March 16th, devoted to the master plan consultant.

what_happened.line: The commission reached consensus among its four members that the skate park group will have to provide a bond covering completion or restoration of the site.
The commission voted by roll call to let the chair sign the notice of intent for the Marshall Park septic permitting, to go to the engineer for the conservation commission.
The chair will ask the town manager what the restoration bond would be called and report back; members favored a bond to avoid prevailing-wage costs to the town.
No action was taken on portable toilets at the parks, and the Marshall Park survey was held until a funding source is voted.
The January draft minutes were held for review, and the next meeting was set for March 16th with the master plan consultant.

why_it_matters: A bond requirement shapes who carries the risk if the skate park is left unfinished, and whether the town could face prevailing-wage costs to complete or restore the site.

Funding for the beach building wall repair and the beach lifeguard line is still undecided, so it is not yet clear whether those costs fall on the DPW facilities line, the parks revolving fund or the town budget.
